in my model, and want to know if I could save the effort to implement a FFT algorithm by my own.

Best regards
Yuping

messages.subject: Nimble webinar Tuesday April 19
messages.body_plain:
Dear nimble-users and nimble-announce,

We'll be holding a webinar on Nimble Tuesday, April 19, with
registration deadline on Friday April 15. Details below.

-Chris

--------------------------------------------------------

ASA Webinar: Programming with Models: An Introduction to NIMBLE, a
BUGS-compatible System for Hierarchical Statistical Modeling Using
MCMC and More

NIMBLE is a new system for programming with hierarchical models in R.
NIMBLE provides analysts with a flexible system for using MCMC,
sequential MC, and other techniques on user-specified models. It
provides developers and methodologists with the ability to write
algorithms in an R-like syntax that can be easily disseminated to
users. C++ versions of models and algorithms are created for speed,
but these are manipulated from R without any need for analysts or
algorithm developers to program in C++. While analysts can use NIMBLE
as a drop-in replacement for WinBUGS or JAGS, NIMBLE provides greatly
enhanced functionality in a number of ways, including customization of
MCMC sampling, user-defined distributions and samplers, and use of
non-MCMC algorithms.

We'll be holding a webinar Tuesday April 19, 3 - 5 pm Eastern. No
previous experience with NIMBLE is required although the webinar will
expect familiarity with the basics of MCMC and with R.

More details are here; the registration deadline is Friday April 15 at
noon Eastern.

http://www.amstat.org/education/weblectures/#PMAINB

messages.subject: version 0.5 of NIMBLE released
messages.body_plain:
Dear nimble-users and nimble-announce,

We're pleased to announce that we've released version 0.5 of NIMBLE at
R-nimble.org.

Version 0.5 is a major release. Highlights include
 - more efficient computations for conjugate sampling,
 - additional automated checking of BUGS syntax to improve NIMBLE’s
warning/error messages,
 - new API functionality to allow the use of syntax such as
model$calculate(), etc. (syntax such as calculate(model) still works),
 - new API functionality for MCMC sampler specification,
 - improvements in speed and memory use in building models, and
 - addition of forwardsolve, backsolve, and solve to the NIMBLE DSL.

More details on the NIMBLE web page and the NEWS file of the package.

Also, we anticipate being on CRAN in upcoming weeks as well as a next
release soon that will include a full suite of sequential Monte Carlo
(i.e., particle filtering) algorithms.

 - Chris Paciorek for the NIMBLE Development Team

messages.subject: compiling with .Machine$double.eps
messages.body_plain:
I'm converting an R function to nimble and trying to compile it. Compilation is failing with either of the two following lines

sc <- 0 + .Machine["double.eps"]
sc <- 0 + .Machine$double.eps

What's the best work around?

Here's a toy example

nf_example <- nimbleFunction(
     ## Example function to reproduce compilation bug
     run = function(a = double(0)) {
         sc <- a  + .Machine$double.eps
         print(sc)
         return(sc)
         returnType(double(0))
    }
)

nf_example(a=0)              ## returns 2.220446e-16 on my machine

c_example <- compileNimble(nf_example)
Error in thisKeywordInfo$processor(code, nfProc) :
  No legal use of dollar sign in nimbleFunction with no setup code

messages.subject: Re: compiling with .Machine$double.eps
messages.body_plain:
We don’t have those system constants for use in compiled code (although it’s an interesting idea that perhaps we should).

For the moment I suggest simply hard-coding a small constant in there.  If you really want to have the code portable across machines, you could use R’s code manipulation features to insert the constant into the code before evaluating it:

myCode <- substitute( nimbleFunction(

      ## Example function to reproduce compilation bug
      run = function(a = double(0)) {

          sc <- a  + DOUBLE_EPS
         print(sc)
         return(sc)
         returnType(double(0))
    }
), list(DOUBLE_EPS = .Machine$double.eps))

nf_example <- eval(myCode)

Perry

messages.subject: Re: equals with a vector
messages.body_plain:
Actually this code does work.  The bug appears to be only in our model checking, not in the handling the model itself.  Please build the model with

nimbleModel(<regular arguments>, check = FALSE)

and you should be able to use it.  Alternatively, you can use

Nalive[i] <- 1- (Nind[i] == 0)

and then you will not need to use check = FALSE when building the model.

Thanks for this report.

Perry

messages.subject: Issue with model building in Linux terminal
messages.subject_clean: Issue with model building in Linux terminal
messages.body_plain:
Hi folks,

I've been using nimble on a Linux machine mostly through RStudio. Recently, I've wanted to run nimble through the terminal using the Rscript command to decrease my total RAM usage for a particularly large model. When I run this particular script through Rstudio it builds a nimble model object with no issues, but I get this feedback when running it through the Rscript command in the Linux terminal:

Loading required package: nimble

Attaching package: ‘nimble’

The following object is masked from ‘package:stats’:

    simulate

The following object is masked from ‘package:base’:

    deparse

defining model...
building model...
Error in newClass(inputList = inputList, name = name) :
  could not find function "new"
Calls: nimbleModel -> BUGSmodel -> <Anonymous> -> modelClass -> newClass
Execution halted

I can't seem to find any information on this error. Does anybody know what the issue is and if there is a fix available?

Thanks very much. Cheers,

Evan Adams, PhD
Ecological Modeler <http://www.briloon.org/about-us/bri-staff/wildlife-research-biologists/evan-adams-m-s-ph-d-candidate>

automatically in an interactive session but not with Rscript. Try
"library(methods)" at the beginning of your script.

Chris

> Dear nimble-users and nimble-announce,
>
> We'll be holding a webinar on Nimble Tuesday, April 19, with
> registration deadline on Friday April 15. Details below.
>
> -Chris
>
> --------------------------------------------------------
>
> ASA Webinar: Programming with Models: An Introduction to NIMBLE, a
> BUGS-compatible System for Hierarchical Statistical Modeling Using
> MCMC and More
>
> NIMBLE is a new system for programming with hierarchical models in R.
> NIMBLE provides analysts with a flexible system for using MCMC,
> sequential MC, and other techniques on user-specified models. It
> provides developers and methodologists with the ability to write
> algorithms in an R-like syntax that can be easily disseminated to
> users. C++ versions of models and algorithms are created for speed,
> but these are manipulated from R without any need for analysts or
> algorithm developers to program in C++. While analysts can use NIMBLE
> as a drop-in replacement for WinBUGS or JAGS, NIMBLE provides greatly
> enhanced functionality in a number of ways, including customization of
> MCMC sampling, user-defined distributions and samplers, and use of
> non-MCMC algorithms.
>
> We'll be holding a webinar Tuesday April 19, 3 - 5 pm Eastern. No
> previous experience with NIMBLE is required although the webinar will
> expect familiarity with the basics of MCMC and with R.
>
> More details are here; the registration deadline is Friday April 15 at
> noon Eastern.
>
> http://www.amstat.org/education/weblectures/#PMAINB

messages.subject: Nimble error
messages.body_plain:
Hi.

I am trying to run a nested multilevel error -- this code worked fine in JAGS, but I'm getting an error message when I try using Nimble.

Any thoughts?

Thanks.

Jim

```{r}
d <- read.csv("http://personal.bgsu.edu/~albert/data/gateway.csv")
library(dplyr)
d$month <- as.numeric(d$Month)
d$year <- d$Year - 2002
```

```{r}
library(nimble)
```

```{r}
worshipCode <- nimbleCode({
  for (i in 1:N){
  y[i] ~ dpois(lambda[i])
  log(lambda[i]) <- mu + epsilon[i] + alpha[month[i]]
  epsilon[i] ~ dnorm(0, sd=sigma.y)
  }
  for (j in 1:J){
  alpha[j] ~ dnorm(0, sd=sigma.month)
}
mu ~ dnorm(0, sd=1000)
sigma.y ~ dunif(0, 100)
sigma.month ~ dunif(0, 100)
})
```

```{r}
worshipConsts <- list(N=484,
                      J=12,
                      K=10,
                      month=d$month)
worshipData <- list(y=d$Count)
worshipInits <- list(mu=5, sigma.y=.4, sigma.month=.4,
                     alpha=rep(0, 12))
```

```{r}
worship <- nimbleModel(code = worshipCode, name = 'worship',
                    constants = worshipConsts,
                    data = worshipData,
                    inits=worshipInits)
```
